resources.string: Detect and configure every motor on the bus: usage, motor size, battery, gearing, direction
Measure resistance, inductance and flux linkage and work out the controller gains
Find the hall sensor table for FOC
Find the encoder offset, ratio and direction
Sensorless BLDC parameters and the hall table
Test each motor on the bus and set which ones run inverted
The motor will spin up. Lift the wheel off the ground or clamp the motor, and keep hands and cables clear.
The motor will turn slowly a few times each way. Lift the wheel off the ground and keep hands and cables clear.
The motor will buzz but not turn while resistance and inductance are measured. The noise is normal. Keep the wheel off the ground in case it moves.
The motor will spin up open loop to the set duty cycle, then coast. Lift the wheel off the ground or clamp the motor, and keep hands and cables clear.
With the current at 0 nothing is driven: turn the motor by hand or with another motor while it measures.
The motor will run slowly for about 2 seconds. Lift the wheel off the ground and keep hands clear.

Stop sends an emergency stop to the connected controller (both motors on a dual board). Whether that interrupts a detection already running in the firmware hasn\'t been verified on hardware, and motors on other CAN controllers keep going until their detection ends.
The controller may still be finishing the current measurement. Wait a little before starting another one; it ignores new ones until then.
The controller didn\'t answer in time
The controller\'s config layout doesn\'t match this app\'s
Resistance and inductance couldn\'t be measured
The flux linkage couldn\'t be measured
Check that the motor turned freely. Try more current, a lower acceleration or a different duty cycle.

Writes resistance, inductance, flux linkage, the current controller gains and the observer gain to this controller\'s motor config (and the temperature compensation base and encoder values when they were measured). The old values are overwritten.
Writes the detected table to this controller\'s FOC hall table.
Writes the encoder offset, ratio and direction to this controller\'s motor config.
Writes the integrator limit, BEMF coupling and, if the halls were read, the hall table to this controller\'s motor config.
The sensor port is set to %1$s
Hall detection only runs with the sensor port set to Hall Sensors (Motor settings, General, Sensors). Otherwise the controller sends no usable answer.
The hall sensors couldn\'t be read
Check the sensor cable and that the motor turned. A working sensor never shows two of the eight states (255 above).
Choose the encoder for the sensor port in Motor settings (General, Sensors) and write it, then detect again.
The BEMF coupling is unusually high; the motor probably didn\'t run properly. Check the result before writing it.
The hall sensors couldn\'t be read
WS2811 LEDs are enabled, so hall sensors can\'t be used
An encoder is enabled, so hall sensors can\'t be used
Sets up FOC on the connected controller and the motor controllers on its CAN bus: what it drives, motor size, battery, gearing, then measures every motor and sets current limits and sensors.
The connected device isn\'t a motor controller and none answered on its CAN bus.
Optional: start from factory settings. Recommended unless these controllers are already set up the way you want.
Writes the firmware\'s default motor and app config to all %1$d controllers. Every setting you changed is lost, including CAN ids and inputs.
The motor size sets the current used during detection and the current limits afterwards. Choosing a class much larger than your motor can destroy it during detection.
Per controller: divide your battery\'s limits by the number of controllers. Regen is negative.
Battery current will only be limited when the pack sags below its cutoff voltage. That is fine for most packs, but check your battery and BMS ratings.
Detection measures each motor and spins it up, then stores current limits, motor parameters and sensors. Lift every wheel off the ground or clamp the motors before starting. It takes about a minute.
Detect all motors on the CAN bus
The motor will spin up several times during the next minute. Every wheel must be off the ground and nothing near the motor.
Every motor on the CAN bus will spin up several times during the next minute. Every wheel must be off the ground and nothing near the motors.
A fault stayed active. Check the realtime data for the fault code.
The flux linkage couldn\'t be measured. Check that the motor turned freely and the motor size matches.
A controller on the CAN bus didn\'t report back in time.
Detection failed on a controller on the CAN bus.
It stopped without a fault code, for no reason the firmware reports.
Detection finished and the results are stored
Run each motor briefly to see which way it turns, and switch on Inverted for the ones that run the wrong way.
